findings.summary: Wallet credit can commit while return transition later loses a race
findings.details: processVendorConfirmation loads the return without a pessimistic lock, calls walletMutationDelegate.doReturnCreditInTx(...) in REQUIRES_NEW, and only then saves RETURN_CONFIRMED. A concurrent vendor rejection webhook or admin reject/resolve path can save RETURN_REJECTED before the confirm path saves; because the credit already committed in the separate transaction, an optimistic-lock failure or rollback on the return save leaves the user credited while the return is rejected.
findings.recommendation: Serialize terminal return transitions with a pessimistic lock by vendor reference/id, and do not commit the wallet credit in a separate transaction before the return transition is durable. Prefer one atomic transaction for state+ledger or an outbox/state-machine step.

findings.summary: Vendor notification can hang forever and bypass retry/DLQ handling
findings.details: ReturnVendorService constructs a default RestTemplate and calls postForObject from an async worker. With no connect/read timeout, a stalled Xoxoday connection can block the worker indefinitely; the retry loop and DLQ route only run after an exception, so blackholed dependencies can exhaust the async executor.
findings.recommendation: Inject a configured HTTP client with bounded connect/read/response timeouts, make timeout values configurable.
